questions.q: What does an AMI actually contain?
options: Only a list of installed software, with no disk data
A root volume snapshot, launch permissions, and a block device mapping
A running copy of every instance ever launched from it
A billing record of past EC2 usage
questions.explain: An AMI is a template: the OS/software snapshot that becomes the root volume, who's allowed to use it, and how volumes attach.

questions.q: What does aws ec2 create-image do?
options: Captures an instance's current disk state as a new, reusable custom AMI
Permanently deletes an AMI from the account
Launches a brand-new instance from an existing AMI
Changes an instance's instance type
questions.explain: create-image lets you turn a configured instance into a template so future launches start from an identical, known-good state.

questions.q: Which EC2 lifecycle state means an instance is off, but you're no longer billed for compute?
options: stopped
shutting-down
pending
terminated
questions.explain: stopped means the instance is powered off and compute billing has stopped, but the root EBS volume still exists and still costs storage money.

questions.q: What is the key difference between stopping and terminating an EC2 instance?
options: Terminating can be undone with start-instances; stopping cannot
Stopping preserves the root EBS volume; terminating deletes it by default
There is no real difference — both commands do the same thing
Stopping deletes the instance permanently; terminating just powers it off
questions.explain: stop-instances keeps the root volume intact so you can start the instance again later; terminate-instances deletes the instance and, by default, its root volume too.

questions.q: What controls whether an instance's root EBS volume is deleted when the instance is terminated?
options: The region the instance is running in
The volume's DeleteOnTermination flag
The instance type the instance was launched with
Whether the instance was ever stopped first
questions.explain: DeleteOnTermination defaults to true for the root volume, so it's deleted along with the instance unless you explicitly set that flag to false beforehand.
